headline: On paper they look identical
body: So letrozole and anastrozole are both non-steroidal aromatase inhibitors. Same drug class, same enzyme target, similar molecular size, similar physical properties. People swap between them like they are the same compound at a different dose, and for what they do in your body that is roughly fair. | There is one measured difference that makes them completely different drugs above the neck, and it has been sitting in the pharmacology literature since 2013 without reaching anyone who actually takes them.
punch: Same class. Not the same drug.

headline: Someone measured
body: Miyajima 2013 measured the brain-to-plasma ratio of three aromatase inhibitors in mice. That number, written Kp,brain, tells you how much of what is circulating in blood ends up in brain tissue. | Letrozole came in at **0.383**. Vorozole at **0.185**. Anastrozole at **0.0299**. Divide the first by the last and letrozole reaches the brain **12.8 times** more effectively than anastrozole does from the same circulating level.

headline: The paper notes why
body: Their own wording is that anastrozole's level was lower than the other two **despite their similar physicochemical properties**. That phrase is doing a lot of work. | Chemically, these three molecules should cross a membrane at broadly comparable rates. Size, lipophilicity and charge all predict similar behaviour. They do not behave similarly, which means something active is creating the gap rather than passive diffusion failing.
punch: Chemistry says the same. Biology says otherwise.

headline: So why the difference?
body: **Anastrozole and vorozole were transported by P-glycoprotein**, an efflux pump embedded in the blood-brain barrier whose entire job is recognising foreign molecules and throwing them back into circulation. | Knock that pump out genetically and anastrozole's brain level rises **12-fold**. So the barrier was never blocking anastrozole passively. The barrier was actively removing it, continuously, as fast as it arrived.
punch: _There is a pump, and anastrozole is its customer._

headline: Uptake tells the same story
body: They checked it a different way, perfusing the brain directly and measuring uptake clearance. Anastrozole **0.108**, letrozole **0.422**, vorozole **0.910**. Same ranking, different technique, which is what you want before believing a result. | The authors' conclusion is unambiguous: active efflux limits anastrozole in the central nervous system, **whereas vorozole and letrozole easily traverse the barrier**.
punch: One goes in. One gets thrown out.

headline: Why does brain aromatase matter?
subhead: YOUR BRAIN MAKES ITS OWN ESTROGEN
body: Aromatase is not only in fat and gonads. The brain runs its own aromatase and manufactures estradiol locally in regions including the hippocampus, using it right where it is made. | That local estrogen is involved in memory formation and in neuroprotection. So an inhibitor that reaches brain tissue is not simply lowering a number on a blood panel. It is shutting down a local production system in an organ you were not aiming at.
punch: *Local* estrogen again. A different tissue, the same lesson.

headline: Which means they diverge
body: At clinical doses letrozole reaches brain concentrations **above** the aromatase IC50, the threshold at which the enzyme is genuinely inhibited rather than nudged. | Anastrozole reaches brain concentrations **below** it. So one of them suppresses brain aromatase and the other largely leaves it running, while both do the same job in the rest of the body. Same peripheral effect, opposite central effect.
punch: ==Same peripheral job. Opposite effect on brain estrogen.==

headline: There is rodent data
body: In a rat model of cerebral ischemia, letrozole **increased infarct volume and caused seizures** in intact male rats. That is a severe outcome in an acute injury model. | It is one rodent model of one specific insult and it is not a prediction about what happens in a healthy person taking an AI. It is still the direction you would expect if locally made brain estrogen is protective, which is the hypothesis it was testing.
punch: Rodent. Acute insult. Worth knowing anyway.

headline: In humans the signal
body: Clinical studies in women treated with aromatase inhibitors report effects on cognition and memory. That literature exists and it is real. | It is also messy, because the women in those studies are being treated for breast cancer and are therefore confounded by the disease, the surgery, the chemotherapy and the age. The pharmacology above is the clean part of this post. The human outcome data is not.
punch: The mechanism is clean. The outcomes are not.

headline: Be precise
body: The brain penetration numbers are **mouse pharmacokinetics**. What they establish is that two drugs sold as interchangeable behave completely differently at the blood-brain barrier, and exactly why that happens. | They do not establish a human cognitive outcome and nobody should quote them as if they do. The gap between a measured pharmacokinetic difference and a clinical consequence is real and this post does not cross it.
punch: Mouse PK. A mechanism, not an outcome.

headline: What to take from this
body: Two drugs sold as the same class differ **12.8 fold** in brain exposure, because one is a substrate for an efflux pump and the other is not. That is measured, replicated by two methods, and mechanistically explained. | If you are thinking about aromatase anywhere above the neck, these two are not interchangeable, and almost nobody discussing them knows this measurement exists.
punch: ==Interchangeable in the body. Not in the head.==
